title: The corner that rides a circle
hook: Slide a point round a circle. Does the corner it makes get sharper?

knows: that the angles of a triangle add up to 180 degrees
what a circle's centre and radius are
doesNotKnow: that every triangle drawn on a diameter has a right angle at the circle

misconception: The angle at P changes as P moves, so it is sharper in some places than others.
objective: The learner can explain that the angle at P is always 90 degrees: the radius OP splits the triangle into two triangles with two equal sides, so 2x + 2y = 180 and x + y = 90.

claims.text: For any point P on a circle other than A and B, where AB is a line through the centre (a diameter), the angle APB is 90°.
claims.source: Thales' theorem; Euclid, Elements III.31. The stage measures the angle from the drawn coordinates at 17 positions (10° to 170° round from B); node gives 90.000000 at each.

claims.text: OA, OP and OB are all radii, so triangles OPA and OPB each have two equal sides and therefore two equal angles: x and x, y and y.
claims.source: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal (Euclid, Elements I.5). Stage readout measures x and y at P; node confirms they match the angles at A and B (e.g. 15° and 75° at place 3).

claims.text: The big triangle's angles are x, x + y and y, which add to 180°, so 2x + 2y = 180° and the angle at P, x + y, is 90°.
claims.source: Angle sum of triangle APB: x + (x + y) + y = 180, so x + y = 90.

recall.question: A triangle is drawn inside a circle with one side running straight through the centre and the third corner on the circle. What is the angle at that corner?
recall.why: The radius to the corner splits the triangle into two with two equal sides each, so the corner's two parts add to half of 180°: always 90°.
